web_evidence.title: Septiembre — Fragmento
web_evidence.note: Penguin Random House's authorized Spanish excerpt contains the opening two chapters. It sustains third-person narration first around Violet Aird and then Noel Keeling, including externally reported actions, perceptions, and private thoughts; no participating narrator frames either chapter.

search_log: Searched "Rosamunde Pilcher September novel excerpt", "first chapter excerpt", and Google Books preview; found an authorized Penguin Random House translated extract covering Chapters 1 and 2.

Searched "September Rosamunde Pilcher point of view", "third person", and "narrator"; results were mostly catalog summaries or audiobook-reader metadata rather than explicit narrative-person analysis.
Opened the Hachette UK publisher page and followed its Read Excerpt control, but the control returned the same product page without accessible prose.

Checked Google Books editions, a French publisher extract link, Booknode passages, library records, and review results; Google Books offered only limited snippets, the French extract timed out, and summaries/reviews did not independently establish narrative person.
person_note: The book's base narration is third person. Three Goodreads passages independently expose characters' private realizations or plans through third-person external narration/free-indirect discourse, while the remaining I/you material is gnomic, conversational, fragmentary, or otherwise non-base. The authorized opening corroborates this across two chapters and two focal characters, Violet and Noel, without any first-person frame. The main limitation is that the Tier A source covers only the opening, but the interior quote evidence agrees and no credible source indicates sustained first- or second-person sections.
